report.summary: Cross-file analysis reveals three patterns: (1) docstring vs. implementation mismatches across modules, (2) missing type definitions that break contracts, (3) inconsistent handling of edge cases in AST parsing.
risks: Docstring claims in multiple modules are not enforced by code, leading to incorrect assumptions.
Forward references to undefined types (JobLimits, LOW_INTEGRITY_SID) may cause runtime errors.
AST parsing silently ignores PEP 695 type aliases on Python < 3.12, causing missing type declarations.
Sorting on None line numbers in parse.py may crash.
CLASS_STATUS mapping orphan->island contradicts the comment that orphans keep their own name.
todos: Align docstrings with implementation in graph_delta.py, render.py, and spine/containment.py.
Define or import JobLimits and LOW_INTEGRITY_SID in spine/containment.py.
Handle ast.TypeAlias absence gracefully in parse.py or document Python version requirement.
Handle None line numbers in parse.py sort keys.
Resolve orphan status rendering: either fix comment or mapping.

hypotheses.claim: Multiple modules have docstrings that make claims about behavior not implemented in code, creating a systematic gap between specification and implementation.
hypotheses.mechanism: In graph_delta.py, comment claims line qualification but code merges same-named methods. In render.py, docstring claims all Stamp fields degrade to strings but dirty_paths and untracked_scanned default to int -1. In spine/containment.py, docstring claims cancellation ladder mirrors ManagedProcess but no cancel method exists in chunk.
hypotheses.refuted_by: If all docstrings in those modules match the code exactly, this hypothesis is refuted.

hypotheses.claim: The codebase has forward references to types (JobLimits, LOW_INTEGRITY_SID) that are not defined in the scanned chunks, risking runtime NameError if not imported elsewhere.
hypotheses.mechanism: ContainmentAttestation.job_limits uses 'JobLimits | None' but JobLimits is not defined in the chunk. Properties low_token_obtained and worktree_labelled reference LOW_INTEGRITY_SID without definition. These may be imported from other modules but the dependency is unclear.
hypotheses.refuted_by: If JobLimits and LOW_INTEGRITY_SID are defined in earlier chunks of the same file or imported from other modules, this hypothesis is refuted.

hypotheses.claim: AST parsing in parse.py silently ignores certain constructs (PEP 695 aliases, NewType with <2 args) while graph_delta.py also has incomplete AST walking (no line qualification), indicating a pattern of fragile AST processing.
hypotheses.mechanism: In parse.py, _visit uses getattr(ast, 'TypeAlias', None) which is None on Python < 3.12, causing isinstance(child, None) to always be False, silently skipping PEP 695 aliases. Also, _assign does not validate NewType call structure, risking annotation_text(None). In graph_delta.py, _refs_by_function does not qualify by line as claimed, merging same-named methods.
hypotheses.refuted_by: If parse.py is only run on Python >= 3.12 (so ast.TypeAlias exists) and NewType always has >=2 args, and graph_delta.py's lack of line qualification is intentional, this hypothesis is refuted.
